To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Higgs boson search sensitivity is not diluted in the presence of a light exotic Higgs boson; (2) instead the Higgs bosons’ significance plots become broader; (3) the broadening can be used as a probe of the presence of the exotic Higgs bosons; and (4) the broadening is more sensitive to the exotic Higgs couplings than the exotic Higgs mass.

(a) the Higgs boson significance in a given channel can be affected by a scalar state that mixes with it and (b) the Higgs signal significance can be broadened by the presence of a second scalar state.

the presence of a light exotic scalar can dilute the significance of the Higgs boson in searches in the h → W + W − → l ν lν channel, but only if the exotic scalar has a mass significantly different from that of the Standard Model Higgs, and if the branching ratios of the two scalars to the same final state are not equal.
